text:
ella-ops: FYI ticket from AcmeIoT — they say AWS Marketplace invoice line items don't match our Redwood usage dashboard for Mar 12-13. Invoice shows ~12.3k USD, our dashboard shows ~9.8k USD. AWS invoice id: 1111-2222-3333. Can someone triage?

amy-support: On it. Do we have the customer's marketplace order id and the cloud_account_id?

ella-ops: order_id: ama-ord-67890, cloud_account: aws-acc-999. They included the invoice pdf and our usage export. Sending both to the thread. :paperclip:

raj-sre: Quick hypothesis — marketplace aggregates line items differently: they sometimes bill by SKU/hour and include rounding or minimum granularity. Also check if embeddings were billed under a separate SKU (we report embeddings + generation as tokens in the dashboard by default).

tom-sales: Customer claims they didn't use embeddings heavily, but they did enable vector-search for one microservice. Could that be enough to explain the delta?

ella-ops: I exported our usage for the same window (UTC):
```
date,route,tokens_in,tokens_out,model,unit_cost_usd
2026-03-12T00:00Z,/api/generate,1,1200,gpt-neo-compat,0.0001
2026-03-12T01:00Z,/api/embed,1,3000,embed-128,0.00006
```
Totals from our export: 9,872,341 tokens -> billed $9,872.34 (rounded).

amy-support: I pulled the AWS line items CSV that Acme attached. Snip of relevant rows: 
```
StartTime,EndTime,ProductCode,UsageType,UsageQuantity,Charge
2026-03-12T00:00:00Z,2026-03-12T01:00:00Z,RedwoodInference,gen-tokens,1200,0.12
2026-03-12T00:00:00Z,2026-03-12T01:00:00Z,RedwoodInference,embed-requests,1,3.00
2026-03-12T00:00:00Z,2026-03-12T01:00:00Z,RedwoodInference,embed-tokens,3000,0.18
```
Note AWS shows embed requests as a separate charge ($3.00) — that doesn't map 1:1 to our token-unit pricing.

raj-sre: Two concrete differences to check: timezone/windowing (AWS may bill in customer local timezone vs our UTC buckets) and metering dimension mismatch (AWS has both request-count SKUs and token SKUs). Also rounding/price-per-unit granularity — marketplace may apply a per-request flat charge for embed calls.

ella-ops: I ran a quick reconciliation script: 
```sql
SELECT date_trunc('hour', usage_time at time zone 'UTC') as hour, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM redwood_usage
WHERE cloud_account_id='aws-acc-999' AND date between '2026-03-12' and '2026-03-13'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour;
```
The per-hour tokens align with our export. The delta of ~2500 USD appears in rows labelled "embed-requests" in AWS.

amy-support: Customer says they were charged for 12,000 embed requests (AWS shows 12k x $0.25 = $3,000). Our system logs show 11,994 embed calls for a single route but we don't put a per-request flat charge on embeds — we charge by embed tokens. That suggests our marketplace SKU mapping during onboarding created an extra per-request SKU.

tom-sales: Did we ever ship a per-request SKU for Marketplace accounts? I thought we only expose token SKUs.

raj-sre: Historically we added a temporary per-request metering SKU for early embed alpha (to capture heavy vector search overhead). It should have been disabled for GA customers but maybe this account ended up with that SKU. Check account's marketplace mapping table: `marketplace_metering_skus`.

ella-ops: Checking now — found mapping: aws-acc-999 -> skus: [redwood-gen-tokens, redwood-embed-tokens, redwood-embed-requests-alpha]. That explains the extra invoice line. Looks like provisioning script didn't remove the alpha SKU for this marketplace subscription.

amy-support: Proposed next steps: 1) Confirm quantity stamped by AWS for embed-requests (amy will validate against their invoice xml). 2) Refund / credit discussion with finance if it's our mis-provisioning. 3) Remove alpha SKU from the customer's mapping to prevent future charges. 4) Audit other marketplace customers provisioned in same time window.

raj-sre: I'll write a small audit query to find other accounts with the alpha SKU: 
```
SELECT account_id FROM marketplace_metering_skus WHERE sku LIKE '%embed-requests-alpha%';
```
If >0 results we need a bulk remediation plan.

amy-support: I've escalated to billing-bot and finance. tagging @billing-bot to create a ticket: invoice-1111-2222-3333 investigation. :rotating_light:

billing-bot: Created ticket FIN-2026-089 for invoice 1111-2222-3333. Assigned to @finance (priority: high).

ella-ops: Customer update draft: "We found an unintended per-request SKU attached to your marketplace subscription that caused extra charges. We're working with finance to correct this and will issue credits if appropriate. We've removed the SKU to prevent future charges." Can someone review?

tom-sales: Looks good. Add estimated timeline: "we expect an update within 3 business days".

amy-support: Putting the customer on an immediate credit hold while finance investigates. I'll follow up with a reconciliation export once FIN-2026-089 is resolved.

raj-sre: Action items for eng: add a provisioning check to prevent alpha SKUs being attached to GA accounts (PR and tests). I'll create the ticket.

ella-ops: Thanks all. Closing loop in this thread once finance confirms credit. :thumbsup:
